sermon.title: The Falling Away
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this fourth session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews eleven present truths about the last days and then examines the falling away. He describes how the medieval church fell away from the simplicity of Christ, the good news and godly living, and asks hearers to see how many of the same things are happening in Catholic and Protestant churches in America and Europe today, saying the remnant who keep God’s commandments are the hope.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: This is the fourth session on “present truth.” Two reformers’ names at 18:56 were not clear in the captions and are marked [unclear]. The dates he gives for medieval practices (e.g. 500, 600, 607, 709, 786, 950, 1079 and 1215 AD; the holy water date at 13:59 is spoken unclearly as “18850 rather AD”) and his claims about medieval and modern clergy are given as spoken and have not been checked.

chunks.section_question: Who can forgive sin, and is any church leader infallible?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Bible plainly says only Jesus can forgive sin, while Protestants confess and go right ahead and sin. He says tradition, church articles of faith, false science and famous authors are elevated above Scripture, and that Jesus is the only infallible one, the head of the church; even the reformers could not agree.
chunks.text:
Well, the Bible plainly says that only Jesus can forgive sin. Plainly says that only he has the authority, you know. Now, Protestants, oh yeah, they confess, but they just go right ahead and sin. Ah, Lord, forgive me for being angry. And then 10 minutes later, they’re angry again. Lord, forgive me for committing adultery. Then two days later, they’re committing adultery again. Tradition is equal to the Bible. That means the church rules and regulations, the church articles of faith is equal to Bible truths. Today, Christians have their own opinions that they elevate higher than the scriptures. They elevate their church’s articles of faith.

If my church says it, it’s got to be it. They elevate science, false science, above scripture. They elevate book authors, famous people, above scriptures. We’re doing the same thing. The infallibility of the pope. Folks, the Bible plainly says that Jesus was the only infallible one. He is our shepherd. He is our king. He is our prophet. He is our Lord. He’s the one we follow. He’s the head of the church. There is no spiritual leader or church that is infallible. Don’t let anybody tell you differently. We got to go back to Jesus. Luther, Calvin, [unclear], [unclear], Brown, Smith, and other reformers couldn’t agree. Even when God started restoring things and bringing times of refreshing, these guys couldn’t agree.

chunks.section_question: How did the church fall from godly living into corruption?
chunks.short_answer: He says the early church stood for God and holiness, but medieval leaders lived luxuriously on poor members’ money, sold indulgences, offices and relics, and required pilgrimages. He says TV and radio ministers do the same today, that being rebaptized in the Jordan is ridiculous because one baptism is all the Bible allows, and that sexual immorality was rampant among medieval priests.
chunks.text:
Calvin tried to unite them, but he had the predestination doctrine, which they didn’t agree with. Most of them were in division over the communion table and water baptism at this point. You can’t get any unity over silly things that really is between the person and God. It doesn’t hurt anybody. Now, let’s look at the falling away from living godly to corruption. Okay, the early church was a godly church. They stood, these apostles stood for God and holiness. The medieval church, the leaders lived luxuriously. I mean, they lived in castles, fancy clothes and everything on the members money who were peasants and barely making it.

They sold indulgences, as we said before, to build churches and live high. We do it with books, trinkets, prayers, DVDs, you know, music groups. We just we don’t call them indulgences. We do that today, especially Protestants. Pilgrimages for sin. That’s a punishment. Well, if you want to really be forgiven for your sin, you got to take a pilgrimage and so forth. And then at the end of that pilgrimage, they had relics like a straw from the manger and the a piece of wood from Christ’s cross and a burning bush twig that they paid to see so they could build and live luxury.

He says Bible morality may be unpopular but the results are indisputable; we need to repent, and the remnant of Revelation 12:17, who keep God’s commandments and have the testimony of Jesus, are our hope to turn America back.
chunks.text:
The the Christian church today just uses profanity like it’s no big deal. The actors in the movies do it. We do it. So what? It’s the language of the day. Sorcery. You know, the horoscope, you know, where am I from? Am I a bull? Am I, you know, where was I born and what’s going to happen today? And all this stuff. Witchcraft was rampant in the medieval times and today. Violence. Christians are violent. They’ll beat you up in a minute if you cross their their uh temper. Gambling. faqs.question: What are the three biblical reasons for persecution?
faqs.answer: He says preaching the kingdom of God and repentance, living godly, which threatens people’s lifestyle, and simply believing in Jesus; persecution for doing wrong has no profit or reward.

faqs.question: Do prophets who predict the second coming profit from it?
faqs.answer: He says these false prophets make a fortune off people in the church who think they have some kind of revelation that God says we do not have.

faqs.question: What should you do when you are down?
faqs.answer: He says get back up: we are in the seasons of refreshing and restoration, and God will refresh you and restore you.

faqs.question: How does he compare “once saved, always saved” with last rites?
faqs.answer: He says Protestants made it even easier than last rites: “once saved, always saved,” so nothing could take away my salvation.

faqs.question: Do you need apologetics to answer Bible difficulties?
faqs.answer: He says if you have had an encounter with God, questions like how many times the rooster crowed will not bother you; when you have not, you need apologetics to solve your problems.

faqs.question: Do Protestants do the same things they criticize in Catholics?
faqs.answer: He says yes, in another disguise: TV and radio evangelists sell Jordan River water, olive oil and prayer cloths, and Protestants ask peers instead of praying to dead saints.

faqs.question: Why couldn’t the reformers agree?
faqs.answer: He says most of them were divided over the communion table and water baptism, silly things that are between the person and God and do not hurt anybody.

faqs.question: Should you be rebaptized in the Jordan River?
faqs.answer: He says it is ridiculous: you cannot kill Christ twice, and one baptism is all the Bible allows.

scriptures.text_nkjv: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

faqs.question: Is Bible morality worth it if it is unpopular?
faqs.answer: He says Bible morality may be unpopular, but the results are indisputable.
